artworks.title: Study of the Allegorical Figure Bellona in Rubens' "The Apotheosis of Henri IV"
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows a sketch of a reclining figure on a flat surface. The person is lying on their side, with the head resting on an arm underneath. The sketch depicts the body with soft, curved lines and captures the fluidity of the pose. The facial features are not clearly defined, and the head is turned slightly upward with wavy hair. The figure appears unclothed, with no visible accessories or objects. The background is a blank page, indicating that the drawing is contained within a sketchbook.

artworks.title: Study of the Allegorical Figure France in Rubens' "The Exchange of the Two Princesses"
artworks.medium: graphite and pen and brown ink on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The sketch depicts part of a human figure in a reclining or falling position, primarily showing the upper body. The left arm is extended downward, and the body is angled. The facial features are indistinct, with the head turned slightly to the side. The hair is loosely sketched. The person appears unclothed, with no identifiable accessories. The background is a plain, unadorned sketchbook page.

artworks.title: Study of an Angel in Rubens' "The Prophet Elijah"
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows a sketch of a person's upper body in a reclining position. The person is leaning on their right arm while the left arm is bent alongside the head. The face has subtle features, with indications of the eyes, nose, and lips. The hair is drawn with flowing lines. The person is depicted nude, with shading for contours and shadows. There are no visible accessories, and the background is blank.

artworks.title: The Mill
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: This image shows a pencil sketch depicting a building partially hidden by trees and foliage. The viewpoint appears slightly elevated. The building is central in the composition, with visible windows and structural details. The sketch features loose pencil strokes, creating a soft depiction of the scene. The color palette is monochromatic, with varying shades of gray against off-white paper, creating contrast between light and shadow. Background trees and foliage are suggested with light pencil marks.

artworks.title: Two Studies for "The Judgement of Paris" or "The Amorous Shepherd"
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image displays swirling, curvilinear lines and forms creating an abstract composition. The shapes resemble dynamic figures that may suggest dancers or statuesque poses. The sketch depicts an intricate web of overlapping lines, evoking intertwined human figures engaged in a rhythmic dance, giving an impression of motion and fluidity.

artworks.title: Spanish Dancers
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: Two dynamic figures are depicted in motion. The sketch showcases figures caught in action or dance, with flowing movements suggested through fluid lines and the motion of their limbs and attire. The figures are rendered with quick, expressive pencil strokes that capture a sense of dynamism and energy. The left figure has an upright posture with an extended arm, suggesting mid-run. The right figure also appears active and poised, with one arm raised above the head and the other extending outward. Loose, gestural lines emphasize movement and form in the lively and impressionistic sketch.

artworks.title: Study for "The Judgement of Paris" or "The Amorous Shepherd"
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows swirling and curving lines forming abstract shapes resembling human figures in motion. The pencil strokes vary in thickness, creating a sense of movement throughout. It depicts a dynamic scene with figures engaged in what appears to be a dance or interaction, with limbs outstretched and bodies in motion.

artworks.title: Victor Chocquet and an Angel for "The Apotheosis of Delacroix"
artworks.medium: graphite and pen and brown ink with watercolor on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: This image shows two sketches of figures in reclining positions on a page in a sketchbook. The figure on the left is lying sideways with the head resting on an arm, drawn with loose lines and suggested clothing. The right figure is upside down, reclined with emphasis on the head and upper body, with features indicating closed eyes and wavy hair. Both figures are depicted with minimal details in shades indicating clothing. The background is the off-white paper of the sketchbook.

artworks.title: Peonies
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image depicts a pencil sketch of leaves and a cluster of flowers or foliage on a cream-colored paper. The color palette is mainly shades of gray. The largest cluster of flowers is towards the right-center, drawn with curved lines suggesting petals or dense leaves. The leaves are more spread out and extend towards the top left.

artworks.title: Pelicans
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows a collection of sketched lines and shapes, with overlapping curved forms and some angular strokes. The composition resembles wispy smoke or delicate petal outlines, suggesting floral elements. The lines convey organic movement, similar to light and shadow over a stream.

artworks.title: Thistle
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a budding flower on a stem with leaves. The sketch is done in pencil on a slightly textured paper, featuring a single, prominently rendered flower bud at the end of a stem. The lines are expressive and fluid, giving movement to the leaves and petals surrounding the bud. The background of the drawing is plain, focusing attention on the central floral subject, and it captures the organic curves and shapes of the flower and its foliage. The drawing has a natural and spontaneous feel.

artworks.title: A Nude and Foliage
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image features a sketch on aged paper. On the right side, there is an outline of a human figure focusing on the lower back and legs, with arms bent upwards near the head. On the left side, there are abstract gestural strokes in dark pencil forming a cluster resembling folds or fabric. The pencil lines vary in thickness and shading, providing depth to the abstract shapes. The sketchbook spine is visible along the left edge.

artworks.title: Three Heads, One of Madame Cezanne
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image features two head studies sketched on a paper. On the left, a partial left profile view of a head is shown with the outline of an ear and short hair. On the right, a frontal view of a face with short, parted, and combed back hair is depicted. The drawings focus solely on the head without any indication of clothing or surroundings. The sketches are drawn in pencil on a plain background, with the edges of the paper visible at the top and bottom.

artworks.title: A Man seen from Behind
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows light pencil lines and curves forming an abstract composition. Several short, darker lines cluster to the left resembling a small seated figure. Intersecting lines and curves near the center suggest angular structures. To the right, a faintly sketched arc could be seen. The drawing creates open space for interpretation, inviting connections to familiar shapes while remaining abstract.

artworks.title: The Artist's Son Reading
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows a pencil sketch of a person's head and shoulders. The individual is depicted with their face on their forearm or a surface, indicating a reclining or sleeping position. The person's closed eyes and serene expression are detailed with shading and lines. Their hair is neatly styled with fine strokes for texture. The sketch features loosely drawn clothing, with sparse details. The background is blank, and the page number 63 is visible in the top right corner, with markings in the bottom right corner, suggesting it is part of a sketchbook.

artworks.title: House Surrounded by Vegetation
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: This image is a sketch depicting a landscape scene. The sketch shows a perspective looking slightly downward at various elements. On the right side, faintly outlined structures resembling classical columns are visible. In the middle, abstract shapes suggest trees or foliage with loose pencil strokes. The foreground is less defined, with hazy lines indicating shrubs or ground cover. The sketch uses a monochromatic palette of graphite varying in density for depth and texture.

artworks.title: Figure Resting Head on Hand
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The sketch depicts the upper body of a person. The individual is reclined, with their head resting on one hand. The face shows closed eyes and relaxed lips, with short, tousled dark hair. Minimal details are given to clothing, and no jewelry or objects are shown. The background is a plain, blank page from a book or sketchbook, with a visible binding and numbered corner.

artworks.title: Near the Pool at Jas de Bouffan
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image depicts a sketch of a natural scene with trees viewed from a frontal perspective. There are vertical elements, likely trees, dominating the composition, suggesting a wooded area. The artist uses loose pencil strokes to create a textured effect, depicting foliage and tree trunks. The color palette is monochromatic, with soft graphite hues on a pale background, enhancing shading. The scene appears simple, focusing on capturing the essence of nature with minimal detail.

artworks.title: Man Bending Forward
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image is a pencil sketch of a person lying down. The individual's head is turned slightly to one side and only the top portion of the body is visible up to the shoulders. The person's hair is short and has a slight wave or texture. Their eyes are closed. The person is depicted wearing a simple garment with no visible details of jewelry. There is no intricate background, just the blank page of the sketchbook around the drawing.

artworks.title: Study of the Allegorical Figure of the Genius of Health from Rubens' "The Birth of Louis XIII at Fontainbleau"
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows a sketch of a person in a reclining position, represented from head to toe. The individual is lying on their back with limbs extended in various directions. The facial features are basic, with a simple outline and faint indications of features, while the hair is illustrated with flowing lines. The person is nude, without any clothing or accessories. The background is formed by the open sketchbook's blank page, revealing the paper's edges and the book's spine.

artworks.title: Study of Puget's "Milo of Crotona"
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image is a pencil sketch of two human figures engaged in a wrestling pose. Both figures appear to be male and are fully visible in a dynamic stance. One figure is leaning over the other, gripping or supporting the other's torso. The focus is on their muscular forms, with detailed contours of their limbs and torsos. Facial features are minimally detailed. The figures are depicted without clothing or visible hair. There are no jewelry or objects in the sketch. The background is plain, consisting only of the texture of the blank paper, emphasizing the focus on the figures' interaction.

artworks.title: Study of a Standing Male Figure after the Antique
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image is a sketch of a pair of hands with fingers intertwined, drawn on a blank page in a bound notebook. The hands are depicted in a relaxed position with soft lines and shading defining the fingers. The page is mainly empty, emphasizing the hands, and there are no clothing details. The background is the textured paper of the notebook.

artworks.title: Study of Desiderio da Settignano's "Bust of a Child"
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image is a sketch of a person, likely an infant, in a lying position. The sketch shows only the head and part of the upper body. The face has closed eyes, a small nose, and full lips, with faintly suggested hair around the head. The baby's features are soft and rounded. The sketch has no visible clothes or jewelry, with a plain background and the sketch taking up most of the page.

artworks.title: House in a Park
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image is a pencil sketch illustrating a landscape from an elevated vantage point. The horizon is high on the page, with varying pencil strokes creating depth. The composition is mostly monochromatic, using shades of gray. In the foreground, there is a figure near a body of water, with trees and a distant structure in the background.
